_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Bubble Bobble (NES) - the ADR-0239 selector
sweep (PRD Part A). Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
RUNG 1, NOT RUNG 2, AND THE LADDER WAS CHECKED BOTH WAYS. ADR-0239 s1 says
to use the first rung that reaches the place. Rung 1 is the game's own
selector, by input: the main menu's PASSWORD entry, five letters that arm a
round, and the 1P CONTINUE ROUND screen that commits it. navigation.kind is
'input', so no cheat rides with any session, every session is an ADR-0184 s2
'clean' pass, and all four ADR-0183 surfaces may read the recordings.
Rung 2 IS available here, which is worth recording because a first pass
looking only at the live Data Crystal page concluded it was not: the live
page answers 403 behind a JS challenge (measured 2026-09-26, `curl -sL` ->
HTTP 403 and a 'Just a moment...' interstitial), but the Wayback Machine
holds the article - 'Bubble Bobble (NES)/RAM map', snapshot 20240428033742 of
https://datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Bubble_Bobble_(NES)/RAM_map - and it names
the round outright:
001F            Permanent Frame Counter
0401            Current Level (01 = Level 1)
045D            Super Bubble Bobble switch
0402            Option selected on main menu
0502-0506       Password letters (A-J = 00-09)
002E            P1 remaining lives
So a profile COULD pin $0401 and skip the typing. It does not, because rung
1 reaches every level in the published table and costs nothing but input,
and because a pin is a modified pass while this is not. The same map is
also the independent check on this profile's own reading of the game: the
five-letter array it publishes at $0502-$0506 is the array this profile's
entry scripts were built against, and the 002E lives byte is the one the
measurement below uses to tell 'in play' from 'still on the menu'.
THE SELECTOR, read off this ROM's own screens and its own password routine
(6502 at $FE32-$FFA6, mapper 1, the bank mapped to $C000-$FFFF) and
confirmed with recorded sessions (runs/f1418/bubblebobble/probe, 2026-09-26):
main menu      five entries, walked with SELECT and opened with START:
1P START / 2P START / 1P CONTINUE ROUND / 2P CONTINUE /
PASSWORD. The cursor is $0402 (the map's 'Option selected
on main menu', 0-4) and START leaves it where it is, so
four SELECTs from power-on reach PASSWORD and the menu
itself carries exactly two live sprites.
password       the game holds $0001 = 05 while it is up. Five slots at
$0502-$0506, one letter each, mirrored to the nametable as
the tile index + 0x0A. DOWN advances the letter under the
bubble cursor and is refused at 9 ($FE61), UP takes it back
and is refused at 0 ($FE53) - the letters run A->J and CLAMP
at both ends, they do not wrap. RIGHT and LEFT move the
cursor between the five slots ($FE8D/$FE71, refused at slots
4 and 0). START submits ($FE32). A, B and SELECT are inert
here. A refused password plays sound $23 and restores the
five letters from the backup at $050B-$050F; an accepted one
rings the bell (sound $0D) and writes the round.
EVERY ONE OF THOSE CLAMPS IS MEASURED, not read off the
listing alone (runs/f1418/bubblebobble/probe, 2026-09-26):
eleven DOWNs leave slot 1 at J (r2_D11), DOWN-then-UP leaves
it at A (r2_DU), five RIGHTs leave the cursor on slot 5 with
the DOWN acting there and not on slot 1 (cursor/r5), a LEFT at
slot 1 is refused (cursor/l0), and RIGHT/LEFT/DOWN in sequence
show the field is ADDRESSED by the cursor, not appended to
(r2_RD, r2_RRD, r2_RLD). Read the letters back from the
nametable mirror, not from $0502-$0506: the accepted branch
spends the array, so tst_BBAAB_nostart ends with the array at
AABAB while the drawn row reads BBAAB.
THE THREE-LETTER ARITHMETIC BELOW IS NOT THE ACCEPTANCE TEST.
Ten probes of one shape, AAAA? for ? = A..J (probe/accept5/),
leave exactly one accepted - AAAAB, which arms round 16 - while
AAAAA computes the same 16 and is refused, still on the screen
with the cursor back on the first slot. The last two letters
are therefore constrained by something this profile does NOT
derive, which is why every password here is a published one and
none is synthesised. The constraint is not one string per round
either: round 1 accepts both BBAAB and the Super BBAJI, and
round 112 both EECJJ and EECFG.
continue       after the bell the menu returns with the round armed and the
cursor back on the first entry, 1P START. Two SELECTs reach
1P CONTINUE ROUND; its own START opens a ROUND screen ($CA53
copies the armed round into $86) where A raises the round
and B lowers it ($CAA4), and a SECOND START commits it
($CA80: $0401 = $86) and begins the round. The walkthrough's
own prose is the same step: 'After entering the password, you
can select which level you'd like to continue from by
highlighting the continue portion of the main menu, and
pressing B to decrease, or A to increase, the desired level.'
Measured 2026-09-26, one probe per variant at password AGJJJ:
one START, a 60-frame START, and A instead of the second
START all end still on the menu ($0402 = 2, $002E = 0, two
sprites); the two-START tail ends in play ($0402 = 0,
$002E = 3, sixteen sprites, the round's number in the HUD).
START on 1P START instead begins a NEW game at round 1
whatever the password said - the mistake is one tile away
from looking right, which is why it is written down.
WHAT A PASSWORD DECODES TO. The letters become permuted indices through the
ten-byte table at $FDA1 (0B 0A 12 0F 13 0C 10 0E 0D 11: A->1, B->0, I->2,
F->3, J->4, C->5, G->6, E->7, D->8, H->9) and the accepted branch writes
- ORA, not +: the fields overlap bit 4, so HBGBD is 146, not 162. Both $049C
and $0401 receive it. Every round named below was re-derived with that
formula AND then measured: each session's own final state reads the round
back out of $0401 and $049C.
THE ROUND THE HUD DRAWS IS NOT ALWAYS THE ROUND THE PASSWORD NAMES, AND THAT
IS WHY FIVE PUBLISHED CODES ARE NOT RECORDED HERE. The HUD draws the round
as two tiles, 0x00 + (round / 10) and 0x00 + (round % 10) - no third digit -
and in this ROM's font 0x00-0x09 are '0'-'9' while 0x0A-0x23 are 'A'-'Z', so
round 108 is drawn 'A8'. That is the notation the GameFAQs 'Level Passwords'
page uses for the three rows it prints past the walkthrough's own last level -
'C6 GHCCB', 'E6 HBGBD' and 'F5 HJFAB' - and those three rows are NOT in the
walkthrough's table, whose last row is 'B2 Password: EECJJ Super password:
EECFG' (checked 2026-09-26 against a Wayback Machine snapshot of the page: its
112 rows run 1..99 then A0..B2 and stop there).
Five published codes past the last round were typed and measured, one probe
each (runs/f1418/bubblebobble/probe/), and they agree on a shape that none of
their sources states:
code    where it is published            the ROM computes   $049C  $0401  HUD
GHCCB   GameFAQs, printed as 'C6'         126                7E     7D    60
DDFFI   the codebook's 'Stage Select'     129                81     80    60
HBGBD   GameFAQs, printed as 'E6'         146                92     91    80
HCICD   the codebook's 'Super Game'       153                99     98    80
HJFAB   GameFAQs, printed as 'F5'         155                9B     9A    60
All five pass the ROM's own checksum - the bell rings, the accepted branch
runs, and $049C holds exactly the round $FEF3-$FF61 computes. That is 21 of
21 codes measured: these five plus the sixteen values below, every one of
which reads its own round back out of $049C. What none of the five does is
play the round it names: past the NES version's own last round the
round-to-level lookup lands elsewhere, so the HUD draws 60 or 80 instead, and
THREE OF THE FIVE LAND ON THE SAME LEVEL. $0401 also stops being $049C's twin
there - it comes out one below it in all five - so a session on one of them
would pass a $0401 check while its art belonged to another round, and two of
them would read `new` = 0 against each other, which is ADR-0239 s4's
'did-not-warp'. The letter H is not the problem (the keyboard offers A-J and
the checksum takes it); the round is. They are left out on measurement, not
on the alphabet, and the measurement is in RESULT.md.
THE RAM CHECK, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. Every value checks $0401, the map's
'Current Level (01 = Level 1)' - published, and written by the same routine
that accepts the password ($FF61) and again by the ROUND screen's commit
($CA80). expect is the round in hex. The check is read off the session's own
final state (ADR-0239 s4), and NO address here is pinned, so no check carries
a caveat and the pinned-byte ambiguity of issue #546 cannot arise:
defaults.cheats is absent.
It is the check, not the gate, that says a session arrived (F14.17). A
selector screen draws art, so a non-zero `new` is not proof of a warp: the
password screen's own letters and frame are tile keys the baseline does not
hold, and every session here walks through it. ADR-0239 s4's `new == 0` is
still the did-not-warp gate, and `unique` is still reported for reading.
WHAT $0401 DOES SAY, AND WHAT IT CANNOT. Read off a session's own final
state, $0401 = the round says that round's password was ACCEPTED and armed
- the validator writes it on the accept branch ($FF61), and a refused
password never reaches that write, so a session that mistyped reads 00. It
does not, on its own, say the round was entered: the accept branch writes
$0401 before the continue chain is walked at all. That is measured, not
argued. The probe runs/f1418/bubblebobble/probe/tst_BBAAB_nostart types
BBAAB, submits it, lets the bell ring and stops there: the round is armed
($0401 = 01, $049C = 01) with two live sprites and $002E = 00. The probe
beside it, tst_BBAAB, walks the same password through the continue chain:
HUD drawing '01'. The two states are identical in the byte this profile
checks and different in the ones that say a level started.
So arrival is carried by published bytes that are NOT the check, and
RESULT.md reports them per session: $002E P1 remaining lives (3/2/1 while a
round is played, 0 on the menu AND at GAME OVER), and $040E / $0492, what
the 'Hurry!' countdown is set to for the level and the level's enemy anger
code, which are 00 on the main menu and while the password and continue
chain is being walked, and non-zero from the moment a level starts until the
run ends - the probe probe/ddfi, which dies out and ends on the game's own
post-GAME OVER CONTINUE screen, still reads 11 and 48 with $002E = 00. Both
are one-way - a zero says nothing, and
probe sc_round01 is in play with $002E = 03 and the HUD drawing '01' while
both of the other two still read 00 - and together they cover every session
here: the ones that end in play are proven by $002E >= 01 and the ones that
end at GAME OVER by the $040E / $0492 pair. A value whose $0401 passes and
whose arrival bytes are both zero would be an armed round that was never
played, and this set has none.
A FAILING CHECK IS NOT ALWAYS A BROKEN RUN, and this game has one way to
produce one: the body is blind, so the player can die three times, and a
round that ends moves $0401. The measurement in RESULT.md records where the
sessions actually ended, so a 00 or an advanced round there is read as the
body, not as the entry.
NO LIVES PIN, so ADR-0239 s3's inert control does not apply and was not run.
A pin would have to pass that control byte-identically first, and it has
failed on every game it was tried on; the body is short enough (120 s) that
the GAME OVER screen is a small part of the run rather than the whole of it.
defaults.cheats is therefore absent, and no session is launched with a cheat
at all.
WHAT IS NOT REACHED. A stage that is entered rather than played never shows
the stage-clear transition, and no session here clears a round: the body is
a blind 120 s of jumping and blowing bubbles. So the clear transition, the
bonus round, the round-99 crystal and the four endings (the walkthrough's
'Multiple endings' section) are left to the game's own stage-1 route and to a
later rung-3 measurement that names one. The three 'H' rounds above are left
out for the reason given there. And the walkthrough's 'Identical to Arcade
round N' remarks name ARCADE rounds, not these: they are why three labels in
an earlier draft of this profile (65, 79, 90) were wrong and are now 49, 108
and 111, the NES rounds the same page's own level column gives.
ROM. Every session runs a copy of the dump inside its own output directory,
never the library path, because a folder beside the library ROM already
holds a bootstrap pack for it (generator=mesence-bootstrap/1) and a bootstrap
that finds a textures layer already applying writes nothing. The copies live
in the unversioned runs/ tree; the library file is only ever read.

navigation.label: the main menu's PASSWORD entry (five letters, A-J) and the 1P CONTINUE ROUND screen that commits the round it arms
navigation.source: Bubble Bobble (NES) instruction booklet, 'How to Operate (continued)': 'Password Function' and 'Typing the Password', which are the published description of every step this profile types - the alphabet, the button that moves a letter, the button that moves the cursor, the bell, the refused-password behaviour and the step after it. Read from the 24-page scan at gamesdatabase.org (page 7; image-only, so transcribed with pdftoppm + tesseract and then read as an image; the copy this profile quotes is sha256 a191b7987d48b0d727907acf9f2b69cc). The rounds are the level table on StrategyWiki's 'Bubble Bobble/NES Walkthrough', which prints 'Password :' and 'Super password :' for each of its 112 levels (1..99 then A0..B2, counted 2026-09-26: 99 numeric rows with no gap and 13 letter rows), plus StrategyWiki's 'Bubble Bobble/Secret codes', which writes the level-select entry as 'Level select passwords - EECJJ (Regular) or EECFG (Super)', plus David's Nintendo Code Book's BUBBLE BOBBLE (nes) page, whose own table reads '|B2|EECJJ|' and '|C6|GHCCB|', '|F5|HJFAB|' under a separate 'Super Game:' column holding '|01|HCICD|' and '|E6|HBGBD|' - the same Regular/Super split StrategyWiki draws, from a source that does not share its table - plus the GameFAQs 'Level Passwords' page, which is where the three 'C6'/'E6'/'F5' rows come from and where the letter H first appears - that page answers 403 behind a Cloudflare challenge (measured 2026-09-26, `curl -sL` -> HTTP 403 and a 'Just a moment...' page), so those three codes are cited from the codebook's own identical |C6|, |E6| and |F5| rows, which do resolve. The two StrategyWiki pages and the codebook page were read live on 2026-09-26 (HTTP 200 each; StrategyWiki's `action=raw` endpoint is the part that 403s), and every quote is in _sourcesComment with the URL it came from. ADR-0239 s1 rung 1: input, no cheat. Each password's round was re-derived from this ROM's own validator (the $FDA1 table and the $FEF3-$FF61 arithmetic, in the 16-values + 6-outside-codes self-check of scripts/stages/bubblebobble/password-decode.py, 0 mismatches) and then measured in a recorded session whose own final state reads it back.

_sourcesComment: Verbatim quotes, retrieved 2026-09-26, one block per source. These are the
published inputs navigation.values was built from and the sources its notes[]
cite. The one thing they mostly do NOT say is how the password field is
operated - the booklet is the only one that describes it, and the ROM was read
to confirm it (see _comment).
1. Bubble Bobble (NES) instruction booklet, 'HOW TO OPERATE (continued)',
page 7 of the 24-page scan at
https://www.gamesdatabase.org/Media/SYSTEM/Nintendo_NES/Manual/formated/Bubble_Bobble_-_1988_-_Taito.pdf
(HTTP 200; sha256 a191b7987d48b0d727907acf9f2b69cc). The scan has no text
layer, so the page was rendered and OCR'd and then read as an image; the
OCR prints 'ABCDEFGHlJ' where the booklet prints 'ABCDEFGHIJ'.
'Password Function':
"Each level has a special password which is five letters long and uses
the first ten letters of the alphabet (ABCDEFGHlJ). It appears each time
the game ends. When you turn on your NES, enter the password and you can
start from the last level you played."
'Typing the Password':
"Press the SELECT button to choose the password option and press START.
Use the controller arrow keys (up/down) to select a letter. Use the
left/right keys to move the bubble cursor across the password. Press the
START button. If the bell rings the password is correct. If you're
wrong, the bubble cursor moves back to the first letter of the
password."
"After choosing the correct password, select 1P or 2P CONTINUE and press
START."
2. StrategyWiki, 'Bubble Bobble/NES Walkthrough', live at
https://strategywiki.org/wiki/Bubble_Bobble/NES_Walkthrough (HTTP 200; the
page's own 'last edited on 23 May 2022'; its `action=raw` endpoint answers
403). Its level table, one row per level, 'Password :' then 'Super password
:', 112 rows from 1 to B2. The rows this profile's values name:
"1 Password : BBAAB Super password : BBAJI. Identical to Arcade round 1 ."
"2 Password : BAAAB Super password : BAAJI."   "3 Password : BABBI ..."
"5 Password : BIFFB Super password : BIAJJ."   "10 Password : BCCCB ..."
"16 Password : AAAAB ..."   "20 Password : AFFFB ..."   "30 Password : AGJJJ ..."
"48 Password : FFFFB Super password : FFAJJ. Identical to Arcade round 48 ."
"49 Password : FFIIG Super password : FFBCJ. Identical to Arcade round 65 ."
"99 Password : GEJJJ Super password : GEJAJ. Identical to Arcade round 99 ."
"A8 Password : GBIFG Super password : GBJIB. Identical to Arcade round 79 ."
"B1 Password : GAIFJ Super password : GAJIG. Identical to Arcade round 90 ."
"B2 Password : EECJJ Super password : EECFG."
The 'Identical to Arcade round N' remarks name ARCADE rounds: they are why
three labels in an earlier draft of this profile (65, 79, 90) were wrong and
are now 49, 108 and 111, the NES labels the same page's own level column
gives. The table's last row is B2; there is no C6, E6 or F5 row.
3. StrategyWiki, 'Bubble Bobble/Secret codes', live at
https://strategywiki.org/wiki/Bubble_Bobble/Secret_codes (HTTP 200), NES
section, in full:
"Level select passwords - EECJJ (Regular) or EECFG (Super)"
"By entering these passwords, you can then increase or decrease the
continue level to the desired level that you would like to begin a one or
two player game from."
4. David's Nintendo Code Book, 'BUBBLE BOBBLE (nes)',
http://codebook.potchgult.com/BUBBLE%20BOBBLE%20(nes).html (HTTP 200). The
page stamps itself 'checked-no', which its own arithmetic bears out: the two
codes it puts in its 'Super Game:' column at level |01| compute 153 (HCICD)
and 112 (EECFG) in this ROM, not 1. Quoted:
"checked-no"
"=>Stage Select: Enter password |DDFFI|, and choose a 1 or 2 player
continue round. Press A or B to choose a round."
Its level table (the regular column, then the 'Super Game:' column):
"|01|BBAAB|"  "|02|BAAAB|"  "|03|BABBI|"  "|05|BIFFB|"  "|10|BCCCB|"
"|16|AAAAB|"  "|20|AFFFB|"  "|30|AGJJJ|"  "|48|FFFFB|"  "|49|FFIIG|"
"|B2|EECJJ|"  "|C6|GHCCB|"  "|F5|HJFAB|"
"Super Game: |01|HCICD|  |01|EECFG|  ...  |E6|HBGBD|"
5. TCRF, 'Bubble Bobble (NES, Famicom Disk System)', read from a Wayback
Machine snapshot (tcrf.net answers a JS challenge; HTTP 200 through
web.archive.org), 'Game Select' section:
"The FDS version uses the save function to select the current level
progress. The NES version allows the use of a password system to select
levels."
6. GameFAQs, 'Level Passwords' page: NOT reachable - it answers 403 behind a
Cloudflare challenge (curl -sL -> HTTP 403, 'Just a moment...'). The three
codes this profile measured past the table's last row, 'C6 GHCCB',
'E6 HBGBD' and 'F5 HJFAB', are cited from the codebook's own |C6|, |E6| and
|F5| rows above, which print the same three codes.
